blocks.raw: # Setup Subscription
blocks.text: Setup Subscription

blocks.raw: ## Introduction
blocks.text: Introduction

blocks.raw: Customers can subscribe or unsubscribe from receiving SMS communications for each source of your organization. This module helps you in automating customer subscriptions for InStore, eCommerce accounts, and WeChat.
blocks.text: Customers can subscribe or unsubscribe from receiving SMS communications for each source of your organization. This module helps you in automating customer subscriptions for InStore, eCommerce accounts, and WeChat.

blocks.raw: Two types of subscriptions are supported by Capillary - transaction messages for personalized messages and promotional messages for bulk communications such as campaign messages.
blocks.text: Two types of subscriptions are supported by Capillary - transaction messages for personalized messages and promotional messages for bulk communications such as campaign messages.

blocks.raw: This section provides a detailed procedure on configuring subscriptions for the sources InStore, WeChat, and e-commerce.
blocks.text: This section provides a detailed procedure on configuring subscriptions for the sources InStore, WeChat, and e-commerce.

blocks.raw: ### Limitations
blocks.text: Limitations

blocks.raw:
* Only registered customers can request opt-in or out-out services.
* Success messages for opt-in or opt-out depend on the message you configure on the respective pages.
* When non-registered customers request such opt-in or opt-out service, the request will be silently ignored.
* When a customer who is already opted-in, places a request for opt-in no action will be taken and such requests will be silently ignored.
blocks.text: Only registered customers can request opt-in or out-out services.Success messages for opt-in or opt-out depend on the message you configure on the respective pages.When non-registered customers request such opt-in or opt-out service, the request will be silently ignored.When a customer who is already opted-in, places a request for opt-in no action will be taken and such requests will be silently ignored.

blocks.raw:
> 📘 **Note**
>
> * Supported communication channels are email, SMS, and WeChat.
> * Supported sources are all sources with active accounts that are mapped to the supported channels.
blocks.text: NoteSupported communication channels are email, SMS, and WeChat.Supported sources are all sources with active accounts that are mapped to the supported channels.

blocks.raw: For detailed help on configuring opting in or opting out, see the following topics.
blocks.text: For detailed help on configuring opting in or opting out, see the following topics.

blocks.raw:
1. **Email Subscription Settings**: You can configure email subscriptions through a link that facilitates customers to opt-in or opt-out from org emails.
2. **Mobile Number Subscriptions**: You can configure mobile number subscriptions by two options - either through SMS or missed call.
   * **Missed Call-based Subscription Settings**: In this, a customer needs to give a missed call to the dedicated number that is configured for opt-in or opt-out.
   * **SMS-based Subscription Settings**: In this, the customer needs to send an SMS in the format that is configured for opt-in or opt-out.

blocks.raw:
> 📘 **Note**
>
> * WeChat subscription settings are configured by default (if applicable for the org). You cannot modify WeChat subscription settings.

blocks.raw: ## SMS based Subscription Settings
blocks.text: SMS based Subscription Settings

blocks.raw: The **Capillary Subscription Settings** module lets you configure opt-in or opt-out through a missed call or SMS.
blocks.text: The Capillary Subscription Settings module lets you configure opt-in or opt-out through a missed call or SMS.

blocks.raw:
* For missed call-based opt-in and opt-out, you need to configure different numbers for each action. i.e., opt-in to promotional SMSs, opt-in to transaction SMSs, opt-out of promotional SMSs, opt-out of transaction SMSs.
* For SMS-based opt-in and opt-out, you can have just one number for all actions but with different commands. For example, to opt-out, send STOP to 1234; to opt-in send START to 1234.
blocks.text: For missed call-based opt-in and opt-out, you need to configure different numbers for each action. i.e., opt-in to promotional SMSs, opt-in to transaction SMSs, opt-out of promotional SMSs, opt-out of transaction SMSs.For SMS-based opt-in and opt-out, you can have just one number for all actions but with different commands. For example, to opt-out, send STOP to 1234; to opt-in send START to 1234.

blocks.raw: ## Subscription Message Language Configuration
blocks.text: Subscription Message Language Configuration

blocks.raw: When a user clicks a *Subscribe* or *Unsubscribe* link in an email, a success or failure message is sent. You can control the language of these messages using the config CONF\_ORG\_SUBSCRIPTION\_UPDATE\_MSG. By default, this config is not enabled. To enable, create a ticket with the Capillary Product Support team.
blocks.text: When a user clicks a Subscribe or Unsubscribe link in an email, a success or failure message is sent. You can control the language of these messages using the config CONF_ORG_SUBSCRIPTION_UPDATE_MSG. By default, this config is not enabled. To enable, create a ticket with the Capillary Product Support team.

blocks.raw: ### Behaviour of the config
blocks.text: Behaviour of the config

blocks.raw: The system selects the message language based on the following:
blocks.text: The system selects the message language based on the following:

blocks.raw:
* If the request includes a language code\
  → It uses that language to show the success or failure message.
* If no language code is present in the request, but the config has a default language\
  → It uses the default language defined in the config.
* If the config is not defined at all\
  → It uses English as the fallback language.
blocks.text: If the request includes a language code→ It uses that language to show the success or failure message.If no language code is present in the request, but the config has a default language→ It uses the default language defined in the config.If the config is not defined at all→ It uses English as the fallback language.

blocks.raw: ### Example
blocks.text: Example

blocks.raw:
* **Case 1**: Language code is specified in the request\
  A user clicks the unsubscribe link with the language code set to `Jap` (Japanese).\
  → The success or failure message is in Japanese.
* **Case 2**: No language code, but the config has a default language\
  A user clicks the unsubscribe link without specifying a language code. The config sets the default language to `Jap`.\
  → The success or failure message is in Japanese.
* **Case 3**: No language code in request and no config\
  A user clicks the unsubscribe link without any language code, and the config is not defined.\
  → The success or failure message is in English.

The config sets the default language to Jap.→ The success or failure message is in Japanese.Case 3: No language code in request and no configA user clicks the unsubscribe link without any language code, and the config is not defined.→ The success or failure message is in English.
